name: Paired siblings 2003: stimulus person, six counter-clockwise patterns
origin: Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003 (Laurentian University), circumcerebral "Octopus" ring; Table 1 of that paper
summary: The helmet program for the stimulus person in Persinger's paired-sibling study: six circumcerebral patterns of 5 min each, rotated counter-clockwise, while this person imagines being with the partner, who sits unexposed with EEG in an adjacent room. The paper reports more 5.0 to 5.9 Hz EEG power in the partner during the burst-firing 100-ms pattern (phase 2 here), in four sibling pairs.
notes: Persinger, Koren & Tsang 2003, Table 1 (p.5 [881]): burst-firing 1/1/20/+2, 1/1/100/+20, 3/3000/200/-2; frequency-modulated 1/1/20/-2, 1/1/100/+20, 3/3000/200/-2 (point duration / time between repeats / time on coil 1 / change per coil, ms). Half of the stimulus persons had the reverse order (p.5 [881]). The 5.0 to 5.9 Hz effect came 'only for the burst-firing but not the frequency-modulated pattern' (p.8 [884]); the lab's 2010 review attributes it to '20+2' instead (Persinger & Lavallee 2010 p.9 [793]). This program plays the table in its order; there is no reversed version. A plus sign is played as shorter at each next coil: the lab's own later account of this study has its 100 ms pattern decrease in steps of 20 ms (Persinger 2008 p.10 [16]). Cook 1999 reads the same table the other way (p.3 [63]). The first frequency-modulated pattern plays 20 down to 6 ms: the +2 of the paper's Fig. 1 (p.9 [885]) and of the Richards 2002 table it repeats (p.4 [674]). Table 1 prints -2 for it. The Thomas pattern plays from the 849-point patent table; the burst-firing point values were never published, so the project's rising sweep stands in. One coil at a time, counter-clockwise from Fp1 to Fp2; the site names are this project's reading. Only the stimulus person was exposed, so one helmet delivers the whole magnetic exposure. The paper gives at most 1.5 uT within 1 cm inward from the ring's perimeter and 0.5 uT at its centre (p.4 [880]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. At 1 uT the scalp gets about 24 uT and the ring centre roughly 0.02 uT: stronger at the surface and far weaker at depth. Four pairs, no sham described, single lab, never independently replicated. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Both partners must agree to the experiment. Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on headache, nausea or distress.
setting: Stimulus person: seated, eyes closed or blindfolded, in a closed, quiet room (the lab used a Faraday cage), imagining being in the other room with the partner and touching him or her. Partner: blindfolded in an adjacent room (5 or 10 m away in the lab's later review), with 8-channel EEG over the frontal, temporal, parietal and occipital lobes (for example F7, F8, T7, T8, P3, P4, O1, O2); a 20-s baseline, then a 20-s sample during each pattern, scored by someone blind to which pattern ran.
schedule: Siblings: two sessions a week apart. Strangers (2008): first meet for 1 h twice a week for 4 weeks.
